sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Jacksonville, FL?
sections.html:
You can list it, take a cash offer, or sell as-is to a buyer who handles repairs, and in every case the deed must be signed in front of two witnesses and recorded with the Duval County clerk. Speed depends on the buyer's financing, the condition of title and any liens that need payoff letters.

Jacksonville is large and varied, so the quickest route differs by property. A well-kept house in a sought-after zip code may sell on the open market in a reasonable time. A house needing a roof, a rewire or storm repairs, or one with tenants, probate or code issues, often fits a cash or as-is sale better because the buyer is not waiting on a lender's inspection.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, longest timeline, lender appraisal and repair requests.
  • Cash or as-is: fewer conditions, shorter closing window, you price the condition in.
  • Family transfer: still taxed as a conveyance for money, and the homestead rules below still apply.

sections.h2: What makes Jacksonville different from other Florida cities?
sections.html:
Jacksonville and Duval County merged their governments in 1968, and the city's website calls it the largest city by area in the continental United States. The Census Bureau lists 747.29 square miles of land, a figure that dwarfs most Florida cities, and a July 2025 population estimate of 1,017,689. The city's own page cites about 1,007,189 residents and a 19-member City Council with five at-large seats and 14 district seats.

That size matters when you sell. One municipal government covers beach communities, riverfront downtown, suburban subdivisions and rural edges. Rules for permits, utilities and code enforcement come from a single city, but conditions on the ground vary from block to block.

Housing numbers are more modest than in South Florida. For 2020 to 2024 the Census reports a median owner-occupied home value of $293,700, a 57.6 percent owner-occupied rate and median gross rent of $1,465. Population grew 7.2 percent between the 2020 base and July 2025. The mean commute is 24.1 minutes, and 77,012 residents are veterans. The appraiser's list of exemptions includes several for veterans and service members.

sections.h2: What drives the Jacksonville economy and buyer demand?
sections.html:
The city describes itself as the economic driver for a seven-county Northeast Florida region of about 1.7 million people and as an intermodal hub with port, air cargo, rail and trucking links. It also points to a mild climate and a reasonable cost of living as draws for relocating employers.

Census retail and service figures back up the scale. Total retail sales in 2022 were about $28.6 billion, and health care and social assistance receipts were about $12.1 billion. Those sectors give the city a deep base of local employers.

  • Region: the St. Johns River, historic St. Augustine and Fernandina Beach are all within reach, per the city's regional overview.
  • Households: 394,370 households, averaging 2.42 people.
  • Education: 91.1 percent of adults 25 and older have a high school diploma or higher, and 33.2 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more.

sections.h2: How does the Duval County homestead exemption affect a sale?
sections.html:
Your homestead exemption ends when you sell, and the buyer must file for their own. The Duval County Property Appraiser's office describes a $25,000 exemption plus up to another $25,000 on assessed value above $50,000, with the second layer excluded from school taxes.

The office also explains that a sale resets the picture. When a home is sold, the assessed value rises to market value for the next tax roll, and the Save Our Homes limit of 3 percent or less on annual increases starts again for the new owner. Buyers who are moving within Florida may file for portability, which carries savings from a previous homestead in any of the three preceding tax roll years. Applications are due March 1, and late filing is possible through early September.

The appraiser automatically renews exemptions each January 1 when nothing changes, and mails a renewal card as a receipt. After you sell, the old owner's card no longer applies, so tell the appraiser if you move. Duval's office also publishes a brochure on how short-term renting could affect exemptions, which landlords should read before listing a home they once occupied. For forms, call 904-255-5900 or email pacustserv@coj.net.

sections.h2: What transfer costs and tax dates apply in Jacksonville?
sections.html:
Duval County uses the standard Florida deed tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and all parties to the deed are liable for it under the Department of Revenue's guidance. Consideration includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. The clerk collects the tax at recording.

Recording charges are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with a $1.00 first page and $0.50 additional page trust-fund charge and $4 per page for technology, all under section 28.24. Instruments with more than four names add $1.00 per extra name.

For property tax, the assessment date is January 1, bills arrive in November, and the early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. Taxes become delinquent on April 1. The title agent prorates the year at closing, and you should ask the Duval County tax collector for the current balance rather than estimating.

sections.h2: What if the Jacksonville house has a foreclosure, estate or tenant issue?
sections.html:
• Foreclosure: the clerk sells at public sale between 20 and 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to later. The winning bidder puts down 5 percent, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale. Homestead owners are told to check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale about surplus funds.
  • Probate: summary administration applies when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less or the decedent died more than two years ago. Creditor claims bar on the later of three months after first publication or 30 days after service.
  • Tenants: month-to-month tenancies end with at least 30 days' notice. Nonpayment starts with a three-day written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays, and a tenant who raises any defense besides payment must deposit accrued rent with the court within five days.

Florida does not levy an estate tax for deaths after 2004.

faqs.q: Is Jacksonville's deed tax different from the rest of Florida?
faqs.a: No. Duval County uses the standard rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Only Miami-Dade County differs among Florida counties, according to the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: When is the homestead filing deadline in Duval County?
faqs.a: March 1 each year. The property appraiser's page says late filing is allowed through early September, based on a deadline that falls 25 days after notices of proposed taxes are mailed in mid-August.

faqs.q: Does the buyer take over my homestead benefit?
faqs.a: No. The sale resets the assessed value to market value for the next tax roll, and the buyer must apply for their own exemption by March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell if the house is occupied by a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. Share the lease with the buyer. A month-to-month tenancy ends on at least 30 days' notice, and tenants in a nonpayment case receive a three-day notice that excludes weekends and court holidays.

faqs.q: Who do I call about exemption forms?
faqs.a: The Duval County Property Appraiser lists 904-255-5900 and pacustserv@coj.net on its exemptions page for form requests. The office is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260.
